 Celtics center Mitchell Robinson gets heated at Nets’ Noah Clowney in tense confrontation
 Boston Celtics center Mitchell Robinson and Nets forward Noah Clowney exchange words in a tense first-half confrontation Tuesday night.
 By Josh Davis • Updated Oct 27, 2026 at 9:27 PM ET • 2 min read Add ClutchPoints on Google Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images Boston Celtics center Mitchell Robinson and Brooklyn Nets forward Noah Clowney got into a heated first-half exchange Tuesday night at TD Garden, drawing players and coaches toward the Nets bench during a tense Atlantic Division matchup.
 Robinson and Clowney traded words near the sideline, but the available footage did not show any punches thrown. Robinson received a technical foul during the first half and had seven points and three rebounds as Brooklyn took a 61-56 lead into halftime.
 ClutchPoints shared fan-shot video from Bobby Manning on X, formerly Twitter, capturing the two players going back and forth inside the arena.
 Mitchell Robinson and Noah Clowney going back and forth early in Celtics-Nets 👀
 (via @RealBobManning ) pic.twitter.com/5TS0QSrRMk 
 — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 28, 2026 
 DAZN US later posted the YES Network broadcast angle to the platform, offering another look at the confrontation and the reaction around the Nets bench.
 Things are getting a little chippy between Noah Clowney and Mitchell Robinson 👀
 Stream Every Nets Game on YES with DAZN 📺 #Nets #NBA pic.twitter.com/JeBymni6Rn 
 — DAZN US (@_daznus) October 28, 2026 
 Robinson is in his first season with the Celtics after spending eight seasons with the New York Knicks. Boston signed the 28-year-old center to a three-year, $47.4 million contract in July after he helped New York win its first NBA championship since 1973.
 Article Continues Below The Celtics entered Tuesday at 2-1 after losing to the Detroit Pistons before beating the Knicks and Chicago Bulls. Boston is also playing the second night of a back-to-back after taking down the Bulls 134-99 Monday.
 Robinson opened the season as Boston’s starting center and had said before the season that he expected to play both ends of back-to-backs, a change from how the Knicks managed his workload.
 The sequence unfolded during a physical first half as both teams battled for control. The confrontation remained a verbal exchange, and Boston carried an 86-82 lead over Brooklyn into the fourth quarter.
